conclusion.statement: openpencil (@zseven-w/dsh-openpencil@0.1.0-rc.1) is not compatible with DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 on the author-declared Web plane. All four cells of launch e6036337fe734a3bb26b20338b1fd696 finished with exitCode 0 and no failed tasks, but no plane passed. On the target DSH 0.2.0-rc.1: the native cell openpencil-node24 ended install-failed ('the traced DSH plugin install command failed'), and the Web cell openpencil-node24-web ended surface-incompatible because the install stage exited 1 with an explicit rejection: 'Plugin @zseven-w/dsh-openpencil@0.1.0-rc.1 is incompatible with dsh 0.2.0-rc.1: peerDependencies {@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-locale:^0.1.0-rc.6, @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime:^0.1.0-rc.6, @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-conversation:^0.1.0-rc.6, @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-slots:^0.1.0-rc.6, @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-theme:^0.1.0-rc.6, @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-tool:^0.1.0-rc.6, @deepseek-ai/dsh-fs:^0.1.0-rc.6, @deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver:^0.1.0-rc.6, @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-policy:^0.1.0-rc.6, @deepseek-ai/dsh-session:^0.1.0-rc.6, @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools:^0.1.0-rc.6}'; the exact-version exemption was not active, and registration/host/surface/interaction were all skipped. On the author's own declared baseline DSH 0.1.1-rc.2: the native cell openpencil-node24-dsh-c0ce59f38ddc installed and loaded but is peer-contract-incompatible because react-dom@19.3.0 does not satisfy the plugin's declared ^18.2.0 (a declared-support fact, not proof of a runtime crash), and the Web cell openpencil-node24-web-dsh-259999a30d2a reached install/registration passed but its host stage failed with code 1: 'dsh: user patch-layer watching requires the Cordis HMR service' from @deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot, so surface/interaction were skipped. Both DSH baselines therefore fail before any surface observation; the Web plane was never exercised, and no native, Web/TUI, SDK, or ACP result can be reported as passing. The author's README claim of being 'Tested through DSH 0.1.1-rc.2' is not reproduced by this run. Node 24 was the only evidenced major (CI-pinned 24.11.0, engines >=24.11.0) and was used for every cell; the artifact hash was identical (a4563e560e91bcd3a2a9302ee7dbee046b146c1bd0de6b27b7c7524fd52e77ca) across all four cells, so the failures are not artifact-selection differences. No recovery action was available: the install rejection is a declared peer-range mismatch that only an author-side version bump or an explicit operator-granted exact-version exemption could change, and the 0.1.1-rc.2 host failure is a DSH-side HMR-service precondition, not a plugin defect.
